prompts.promptEn: Take account of yourself today, before you are taken to account.
prompts.citationEn: Athar from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA); cited by al-Ghazali in Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, Book 38

prompts.promptEn: Looking back at your day — what helped you turn toward Allah, and what pulled you away?
prompts.citationEn: al-Ghazali, Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, Book 38 (Kitab al-Muraqaba wa al-Muhasaba)

prompts.promptEn: Which small, consistent act today brought you closer to Allah?
prompts.citationEn: Hadith: 'The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small.' (Bukhari 6464, Muslim 782 — narrated by 'A'isha RA)

prompts.promptEn: Of the actions you performed today, which were truly for Allah's sake?
prompts.citationEn: Hadith: 'Actions are but by intentions.' (Bukhari 1, Muslim 1907 — narrated by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab RA)

prompts.promptEn: Was your prayer today a conversation, or a recitation? What changed in your heart as you stood?
prompts.citationEn: Theme from Ibn al-Qayyim, Madarij al-Salikin (on the station of khushu')

prompts.promptEn: When did you remember Allah today without anyone reminding you?
prompts.citationEn: Hadith: 'The example of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not is like the living and the dead.' (Bukhari 6407 — narrated by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari RA)

prompts.promptEn: Name three blessings from today that you would have missed if you hadn't paused to notice them.
prompts.citationEn: Qur'an 14:7 — 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.'

prompts.promptEn: Where did good come to you today? Where did difficulty come? Did your response in each match the believer's standard?
prompts.citationEn: Hadith: 'Wonderful is the affair of the believer — when good befalls him he is grateful; when harm befalls him he is patient. All of it is good for him.' (Muslim 2999 — narrated by Suhayb RA)

prompts.promptEn: What worry did you carry today that, if you had truly relied on Allah, you could have set down?
prompts.citationEn: Qur'an 65:3 — 'And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him.'

prompts.promptEn: Is there something from today you would not want recorded against you? Turn to Allah now, while the day is still close.
prompts.citationEn: Hadith: 'Allah rejoices more over the repentance of His servant than one of you would over finding his lost camel in the desert.' (Bukhari 6309, Muslim 2747 — narrated by Anas RA)

prompts.promptEn: What habit have you tried to leave before? What would it take, today, to leave it once more?
Where did you reach the edge of your patience today? What carried you across?
prompts.citationEn: Qur'an 2:153 — 'Seek help in patience and prayer; truly Allah is with the patient.'

prompts.promptEn: In this last third of the night, what would you ask of your Lord that you have not yet asked?
prompts.citationEn: Hadith Qudsi: 'Our Lord descends each night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, saying: Who is calling on Me, that I may answer him?' (Bukhari 1145, Muslim 758 — narrated by Abu Hurayra RA)

prompts.promptEn: Sit a moment with one moment from today. What was Allah teaching you in it?
How did you think of Allah today? Did you think of Him as near, or as distant?
prompts.citationEn: Hadith Qudsi: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.' (Bukhari 7405, Muslim 2675 — narrated by Abu Hurayra RA)

framing.pauseModeDescription: Excludes days from your trajectory analytics. The app does not ask why — pause mode is for any time prayer is excused or you simply need a quiet space.
framing.travelModeDescription: Marks days as travel days. Prayer is still expected (qasr or jam' permitting); this just notes that you were traveling.
framing.reflectionEmptySubtitle: Today's prompt is above. Write or speak whatever comes to mind. Past entries appear here.
framing.trajectoryEmptySubtitle: Log your first prayer on the Today screen to start your trajectory.

thresholds.lateDefinitionDescription: A prayer is 'late' when it is performed after the preferred (mustahab) time but still within the valid time window. Ihsan does not enforce a specific threshold — you classify your own prayer based on your own honest assessment.
